look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the rough triangular to broadly ovate leaf blades, usually unlobed or only shallowly lobed, on a long trailing vine. Look for small round, often striped young gourds. This is a perennial from a substantial tuberous rootstock; do not excavate plants merely to verify it. The staged photo shows the leaves, vines and striped fruits, not the underground root.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Long-running, coarse, trailing perennial vine from a large perennial rootstock; stems rough and bearing tendrils.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Alternate, simple, rough leaves, typically triangular to broad-ovate, mostly unlobed or shallowly lobed; do not diagnose by odor alone.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Separate male and female large yellow flowers on the same plant; inspect female inferior ovary below corolla and the calyx/corolla from the side.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Usually small globose gourds around 5–10 cm, green-striped when young and yellowing as mature; compare fruiting peduncle and seed with other Cucurbita.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Trailing rough stems with axillary tendrils; perennial rootstock is a distinguishing life-history character but not safely visible in a normal field photograph.
